scene_plan.assignment: Rehearse the commemorative show and let Kit reclaim the last spoken cue. The running sheet includes a blue comet slide.

review_request.instruction: Read the opening paragraph for the handoff at the cue desk.
review_request.excerpt: At six the front door of Bellweather Planetarium clicked shut, and Kit rang the bicycle bell that stood in for a stage manager. The sound came back from the dome a little smaller. She gave the brass cue key to Ada, who stuck it in the lock with her left hand. Her right was still bandaged from cutting the old show into strips.

saved_review.observation: Kit gives Ada the brass cue key at the start. The sound of the bicycle bell carries through the room.

claims.narration: The scene-four draft explicitly recounts the blue comet being projected onto the planetarium dome during the rehearsal.
claims.event: The blue comet was projected onto the planetarium dome at some time during the scene-four rehearsal.

drafts.open:
At six the front door of Bellweather Planetarium clicked shut, and Kit rang the bicycle bell that stood in for a stage manager. The sound came back from the dome a little smaller. She gave the brass cue key to Ada, who stuck it in the lock with her left hand. Her right was still bandaged from cutting the old show into strips.

On the console lay the blue comet slide in its cardboard mount. A boy had drawn the tail with a scratched needle forty years ago. Ada could feel the burr when she ran a thumb along the edge. On the running sheet the cue had a square beside it for a tick. Someone had sharpened a pencil and left the shavings in the square.

Kit went to sit where the boy used to sit, back when there had still been a boy to bring on Saturdays. The velvet caught at the zip of her coat. Ada tried the first sentence twice. On the second try she let the word “our” take as long as it took, and Kit stopped pulling at the zip.

The two women worked through the middle pages in the hush between the fan and the ticking clock. By the time Kit got back to the desk the tea had a skin on it. Ada held the chipped cup for her while she wrote the final cue in her own hand.

At the closing cue the house lights came up on a blank dome. It stayed blank while Kit rang the bell to end the rehearsal.
